pr.title: Add the VNNI K layout and its readers
Add the VNNI K layout and its readers
pr.head: 82d05e94be

short_version: PR-1 (#4868) stores the saved key vectors (K) of 128-dimension attention heads in the VNNI-packed layout behind a typed owner and typed views, adds the AVX-512 reader and the FPGA staging gather as the two consumers of that layout, and adds no AMX instruction.

The page introduces three data models (the plane geometry with its index map, the typed owner with its views, and the typed kv_block::k with the layout gate) and three algorithms (the per-token scatter store and gather load, the AVX-512 reader qk_group, and the scoring-path selection with the temporary dense gate).

Six base diagrams carry them: kv_cache-b1 (the cache data model), k_vnni-b1 and k_vnni-b1a (the plane), k_vnni-b2 (the types), k_vnni-b3 and kv_cache-b3 (the operations and their call paths); the whole-block store, the page bits and the row-major tail block of the other diagrams land in PR-3 and PR-4.

words.definition: DMA is direct memory access, the engine that moves a staging buffer to the FPGA card. A row view carries two compile-time flags: Aligned says the row starts at a 64-byte boundary, and Dma says the row lives in DMA memory. The K row operations load and store rows with unaligned vector instructions, so they do not require Aligned [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:219-228].
Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set of the CPU. Its tile multiply TDPBF16PS reads its right operand (the B operand) in the VNNI layout. This PR adds no AMX instruction.
The CMake option that compiles the AMX kernels and the code that selects them. This PR does not require it: the option-on build passes its tests with AMX dispatch off.
AMX-on names a run without the kill switch, and AMX-off a run with it (TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1).

The per-page scoring function of h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp. For one (query, page) pair it picks the dense AMX kernel or the software reader. In this PR every page of a VNNI slot takes the software reader qk_group [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1833-1979].

The threads that run the attention kernels of a layer. They read a page only after every minibatch that writes it counted its latch (upstream_kvs_ready) down. Idle attention workers also run the staging gather through help_drain_gof.

Advanced Vector Extensions, the CPU's 512-bit vector instruction set. One register holds 16 lanes of 32 bits. VDPBF16PS is its instruction that multiplies bf16 pairs and adds them in fp32. The reader qk_group, store_row and load_row are AVX-512 code.
bf16 is the 16-bit brain floating-point format of the stored K and V values. fp32 is the 32-bit float format in which the score kernels add. A bf16 shifted up by 16 bits is the exact fp32.

16 consecutive page offsets of a page (BLOCK_TOKENS_16), page offsets 16 c .. 16 c + 15. A page has TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 = 4 blocks. A block's bytes are its 4 panels, 4 KiB in all [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:63-64].
The in-place conversions of one 16-token block between its row-major form and its VNNI form. They land in PR-4 (#4901), not in this PR.
The unit of memory allocation of the KV cache. It owns the memory for a requested number of pages and hands out references to them [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:833].
model.hpp's per-operation answer, decided once per model, whether the FPGA scores the operation's K. PR-4 uses it in save_k to keep such blocks row-major. This PR does not read it in save_k.

The CMake job of .github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml. This PR adds -DTRON_K_VNNI=ON to its configure line, so the whole test suite runs on the VNNI layout there [.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:356].

In save_k, a K buffer row whose activation type is not bf16 is converted to a 64-byte-aligned bf16 row on the stack before set_k_row stores it [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3116-3119]. PR-3 renames that stack array conv.

book::append copies one book's tokens after another's, page by page through page::copy_from, which calls copy_storage_slot per storage slot. Both exist in main and are unchanged by this PR [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1247, 2322].

page::copy_storage_slot copies count tokens of one storage slot from another page. For a VNNI slot this PR copies a whole page as one owner assignment (dst_block.k = src_block.k) and every other range token by token with copy_token (load_row then store_row through a local row) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2286-2301; h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:331-339].
Prefill is prompt processing: many tokens per user per pass. Decode is generation: one token per user per step. The per-token scatter store of this PR costs most in prefill; PR-3 addresses that cost.

A full 64-token page that the query sees whole. main's AMX page kernel qk_rowmajor_128x4 processes it in one call (apply_dense_amx_page). In this PR that path is compiled out for VNNI slots by the temporary gate.

Dimensions 2 dp and 2 dp + 1 of one token, stored together in one 32-bit lane (a dword, DWORD_BYTES_4). The even value is in the low half of the dword and the odd value in the high half [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:59-60].
32 dimensions = 16 dimension pairs (STEP_DIMS_32, STEP_PAIRS_16). A 128-dimension head has DIM_STEPS_4 = 4 steps [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:67-69].

main's per-token dot-product routine for a row-major K row (struct dotter in h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp), driven by the per-token loop of apply_page_tok. In this PR it is compiled only for row-major slots.
A speculation model whose KV storage is one extra physical slot of the book (eagle_storage_offset). This PR does not change it; PR-4 adds a K layout state entry for it.

book::fill_random is a test-only fill of every kv_block with random bf16 values, and fill_storage_slot is its body per storage slot. It is the one documented exception to the typed access rule: for a VNNI slot it takes the plane address through detail::k_vnni_access [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1291, 1716-1726].
The end of one forward pass on the main thread, after the plugin's run() returned and wait_for_coop_gof drained the staging gather. PR-4 converts completed blocks there. This PR converts nothing.
Field-programmable gate array, the card that runs hardware attention and receives K and V rows by DMA.
A group of four consecutive tokens. The staging gather (gof::populate) copies their K and V rows into a buffer that DMA moves to the FPGA card.
Attention scored on the FPGA for an operation. PR-4 adds a policy that keeps short-run blocks row-major under it. This PR has no such policy.

The constexpr function that gives the element index of K[token][dim] inside the plane: (((s * 4 + c) * 16 + dp) * 16 + t) * 2 + j [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:105-112]. The worked example (token 37, dimension 70) gives element 5226.

page_info is the per-token record the scheduler builds for the staging gather. Its k_head_fn callback returns a pointer to the token's K row for one slot and KV head. This PR adds a scratch argument: for a VNNI slot the callback gathers the row into the caller's 64-byte-aligned scratch (256 bytes per head) and returns the scratch [h/tron/gof.hpp:61-78; h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2747-2762].

page::k_packed(slot, kv_head): the read-only typed view (k_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128>) of one page's K plane, VNNI slots only. It is the argument of the reader qk_group [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1991-2001].

The page's two atomic bit arrays per storage slot: one bit per page offset (saved rows) and one bit per 16-token block (converted blocks). They land in PR-4 (#4901). In this PR the page keeps no K layout state.

Helpers that build a read-only row view from a bf16 pointer or from a rank-1 bf16 view that keeps its own flags (k_source_row), and a writable row view from a bf16 pointer (k_destination_row). They neither check alignment nor copy data [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:232-253].

Inside detail::kv_block, k_storage is a std::conditional_t that names k_vnni_tensor<page_size, head_size> when k_vnni::layout_on<head_size> holds and the bf16 array native_k_storage otherwise. The member k has that type. Both hold page_size * head_size bf16 values [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2526-2536].

A friend helper with one static function, plane(view), that returns the view's raw pointer to the plane's first element. It is the only route from a view to a plane address, for the typed operations, the reader qk_group and the test-only fill [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:209-215].

TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 in the environment prevents use of the AMX kernels at run time. With the option on, the switch keeps the layout and the reader: it changes no score and no visit path for 128-dimension heads in this PR [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:707-713].

One key/value head of grouped-query attention. kv_mul is the number of query heads per KV head: 4 for qwen3-4b and llama-3.1-8b, 3 for llama-3.2-3b, and 8 for qwen-3-30b-a3b. The reader scores a group of more than 16 heads in passes of 16.
A KV page is a 64-token block of KV storage allocated by the cache (page_size = 64). The page struct is a lightweight reference into a book [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1826-1828].
The struct that holds the K plane and the V plane of one (storage slot, KV head, page). This PR types its K plane [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2519-2536].

kv_slot_id selects one persistent K/V storage region of the book, usually one per layer [h/tron/attention_ids.hpp:23]. A storage slot (kv_storage_offset) is the absolute physical slot offset in the book's allocation [h/tron/models/common.hpp:240].
One transformer layer of the model. Each layer stores its K and V into its own slot of the KV cache.

k_vnni::layout_on<head_size> is true only for 128-dimension heads and only when the option TRON_K_VNNI is defined. It depends only on the storage geometry, so every reader and writer of a slot selects the same layout [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:95-101].

A 64-bit word with one bit per page offset. apply_page_tok sets the bit of every relevant token during its loop and hands the word to qk_group, which reads only those tokens [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1933, 1962-1963, 1976-1979].

The main thread runs the generated run() of a plugin, including save_k. The main helpers are its helper threads (run_main_help). In this PR save_k runs on main alone; PR-3 shares its K store with the helpers.

mark_k_complete records in the page that a token's K is saved. upstream_kvs_ready is the per-slot latch (a countdown object) that downstream minibatches wait on; save_k counts it down after its stores. Both exist in main and are unchanged here [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3126, 3134-3135].
A deliberate code change that a test must catch. The PR body reports one: removing the per-head scratch offset in gof::populate makes the populate case of t_phase1_integration fail.

The design comment in h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp that says what the layout is, who writes it, who reads it, how each of the six consumers of a VNNI slot changes, and that the kill switch keeps the layout [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:651-713].

words.term: Note [Row-major tail block] / row-major tail block
words.definition: A 16-token block of a VNNI plane whose rows stay row-major until all 16 rows are saved, then converted in place. It lands in PR-4 (#4901). In this PR every row goes straight into the VNNI column.

words.term: Note [Shared block save] / shared block save / window
words.definition: PR-3's design: a run of 16 tokens is stored as one whole block, and the main helpers claim work units of the store through a window of counters. None of it is in this PR.
The page functions that publish the saved-row bits and the block bit. They land in PR-4 (#4901).

The CMake option, default OFF, that selects VNNI-packed K storage for every 128-dimension head [CMakeLists.txt:47]. Its compile definition is PUBLIC on the tron target and on the generated model objects, so every translation unit that touches a KV page sees the same layout [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:232-233, 336-341]. It stays off in every build preset until PR-4.

k_vnni_tensor<64, 128> owns one K plane as a 64-byte-aligned bf16 array, trivial to construct, copy and destroy. k_vnni_view<T, 64, 128> refers to that plane and computes element addresses; at(token, dim) reads one element and cannot write it. Views come only from an owner's as_view(), and a writable view converts to a read-only one, never back [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:135-201].
A token's position inside its 64-token page, 0 to 63. In the VNNI plane the offset decides the token's block (offset / 16) and its column (offset % 16).

One 64-byte line of a panel: one dimension pair for 16 consecutive tokens, 32 bf16 = 16 dwords (ROW_ELEMS_32, ROW_DWORDS_16). The 16 pair rows of a panel are 64 bytes apart [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:24-26, 71-72].

The address arithmetic of store_row and load_row. pair_base gives the byte address of dimension pair 0 of step s for a token (its column in panel (s, c)). pair_row_offsets lists the 16 pair rows of a panel, 16 dwords apart, as the index vector of the scatter and the gather [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:261-281].

One (dimension step s, token block c) cell of the plane: 16 pair rows of 64 bytes = 1 KiB (PANEL_BYTES_1024). A plane has N_PANELS_16 = 16 panels, and a panel is exactly one AMX B tile [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:26-27, 74-77].
The deferred conversion list of save_k and the forward-end function that drains it. They land in PR-4 (#4901).
K for one KV head of one page: 64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB, the same bytes as the row-major plane [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:21-30].

PR is a GitHub pull request of the tron repository. PR 4424 (branch jhan-amx-vnniK) is the original change that the four PRs of the stack replace: PR-1 #4868, PR-2 #4887, PR-3 #4898 and PR-4 #4901, each based on the previous one.
A run with a prompt length of 1024 tokens (runtron --prompt-length). The performance cells of the PR body use prompt 1024 and prompt 8192.

k_vnni::qk_group in h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp: the AVX-512 routine that scores a query group against the live tokens of one VNNI-packed page, one token per vector lane. One 64-byte load supplies one dimension pair of 16 tokens, the query's pair is broadcast, and VDPBF16PS accumulates 16 scores at once, so there is no per-token gather [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:57-126].

qk_rowmajor_128x4 is main's AMX QK kernel for a row-major K page: it puts the K page on the left and transposes the scores on the way out. qk_vnni_128x4 is the AMX kernel that reads the VNNI plane as its B operand and lands in PR-2 (#4887).

The step that rearranges a token's query rows into the AMX operand format (pack_q_group_128x4 in main). In this PR it still runs once per token for a VNNI slot, and no kernel consumes it; the kill switch skips it [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1633-1634, 1688-1696].

A typed view of one token's 128 K values in dimension order, read-only (const_k_row_view) or writable (k_row_view), carrying the caller's Aligned and Dma flags. It is the argument type of set_k_row, get_k_row, store_row and load_row [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:224-228].
One row of head_size bf16 values per token, indexed [token * head_size + dimension]. Every head size other than 128 keeps this layout, and so does a 128-dimension head when the option is off.
tron's command-line tool, the binary the PR body's performance and token-identity runs use.

The function of h/tron/models/model.hpp that stores the K rows of one minibatch into the KV cache. The two save_k overloads forward to save_k_impl. In this PR save_k_impl stores each token's row with page::set_k_row for a VNNI slot and with page::k().set for a row-major slot [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3077-3153].

_mm512_i32scatter_epi32 writes the 16 dwords of one register to a base plus 16 offsets, and _mm512_i32gather_epi32 reads 16 dwords from such addresses. store_row issues 4 scatters per token (one per dimension step) and touches 64 lines; load_row is the inverse with 4 gathers.
The thread that runs the scheduler of h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp between forward passes. It defines the page_info callbacks of the staging gather, which other threads run.
The whole-block store of a run of 16 tokens: 16 rows transposed in registers and written as whole lines. Both land in PR-3 (#4898).

The layout-agnostic page accessors that this PR adds. set_k_row writes one token's row (a const_k_row_view) into whichever layout the slot uses: store_row for a VNNI slot, memcpy for a row-major one. get_k_row is the inverse with load_row [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2010-2063].

The copy of K and V rows of one GOF into the buffer that DMA moves to the FPGA. It runs on an idle attention worker (help_drain_gof) or on main (wait_for_coop_gof). This PR gives it a K scratch array beside the V scratch, with one row per KV head [src/tron/gof.cpp:203-213].

store_row scatters one token's 128-dimension row into its column of the plane: 4 scatters of 16 dwords, one per dimension step, touching only that token's 64 pair slots. load_row gathers the row back. Both check the token index [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:291-322].

The tests of this PR. t_k_vnni_layout is new, with four cases: the index anchors, the exact scrambled store and load, the reader against the dotter, and page rows through store, load and append. t_llama_unit gains the compile checks of the type model, a 32-head compile case and a save_k case. t_phase1_integration's populate case stages K rows through the scratch. t_amx_dispatch_dtype expects no dense kernel call under the option.

The term && !k_vnni::layout_on<operation_head_size> that this PR adds to the dense-page AMX predicate of apply_page_tok. It keeps the dense AMX path out of VNNI slots until PR-2 adds the AMX kernel, so every VNNI-packed page takes the reader [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1885-1887].
Decode throughput in tokens per second per user. The PR body measures a decode TPS loss of 6.4 % at prompt 1024 and 11.6 % at prompt 8192 against main, caused by the temporary gate.
The in-register 16 x 16 transpose that store_block uses. It lands in PR-3 (#4898).
The lock on the scheduler's token tree, held for the tree work between forward passes (clear_kv_complete_at, copy_from).
The inference program under test (the positron-ai/tron repository). Its C++ code lives in namespace tron.

VDPBF16PS is the AVX-512 instruction that multiplies bf16 pairs and adds them in fp32; the reader uses it. TDPBF16PS is the AMX tile multiply that reads the same pair layout as its B operand; no PR-1 code uses it.

Vector Neural Network Instructions layout: two consecutive dimensions of one token are adjacent in memory, and one 64-byte line holds that dimension pair for 16 consecutive tokens. It is the B-operand format of the AMX tile multiply. VNNI-packed means stored in this layout.

The two ends of the cooperative staging gather: idle attention workers run queued GOFs through help_drain_gof, and main drains the rest at the forward end through wait_for_coop_gof. Both exist in main and are unchanged here [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3239, 3252].
tron's record label for the K rows after rope (the rotary position embedding), logged by save_k_impl through log_intermediate [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3094].

The example the three source pages trace through every diagram: the K plane of storage slot 5, KV head 0, page 7, and inside it token 37, dimension 70, which the index map places at element 5226 (panel #10, pair row 3, dword 5).

walkthrough.say: PR-1 is the first of the four PRs that split PR 4424. It stores K of 128-dimension heads in the VNNI-packed layout behind a typed owner and typed views, adds the AVX-512 reader and the FPGA staging gather as the two consumers, and adds no AMX instruction. The CMake option TRON_K_VNNI is off in every build preset, so main's behaviour does not change with the option off [CMakeLists.txt:47]. The compile definition is PUBLIC, so the generated model objects see the same layout as the tron library [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:232-233, 336-341].

Start at the kv_block card: its k member becomes k_storage, a std::conditional_t that names k_vnni_tensor for a VNNI slot and the bf16 array native_k_storage otherwise, with two static_asserts for a trivial type and the same byte count [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2526-2536]. The arrow label is the layout gate k_vnni::layout_on, true only for 128-dimension heads and only with the option [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:95-101]. The row views k_view and k_at exist only on the row-major branch [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2554-2571]. The page's two bit arrays at the right are PR-4, so skip them.

Point at the plane: 64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB, the same bytes as the row-major plane [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:21-30]. Walk the containment: 16 panels of 1 KiB, one per (dimension step s, token block c); a panel is 16 pair rows of 64 bytes; a pair row is one dimension pair for 16 tokens [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:56-77]. Then run the worked example through k_vnni::index: token 37, dimension 70 lands at element 5226 [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:105-112]. The orange frame (block 2 still row-major) is PR-4.

Use the five levels to say the same thing from the top: the K of page 7 for slot 5 is one plane per KV head, a dimension step cuts the columns, a token block cuts the rows, a panel is one cell of the 4 x 4 cut, a pair row holds one pair of 16 tokens, and a dword is one token's pair with the even value in the low half [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:24-29, 59-60]. The hand-computed anchors of this map are the first test case [t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp:101-118]. The last line, the row-major form of a block, is PR-4.

This is the answer to Ben's typed-access request. k_vnni_tensor owns the bytes; as_view() is the only source of a view and is deleted on a temporary [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:180-201]. k_vnni_view reads through at(token, dim) and has no element write, no pointer constructor and no data() [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:135-170]. detail::k_vnni_access::plane is the one route to the raw address, open to store_row, load_row, copy_token, the reader qk_group and the test-only fill_storage_slot [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:209-215; h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:83; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1721-1722]. The transfer rows const_k_row_view and k_row_view carry one token's 128 values in dimension order [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:224-253], and qk_vnni_128x4 in the grey box is PR-2.

Read the register group by group. Groups 1 to 4 are in this PR: the gate and the index map, the views and the access route, the transfer rows with pair_base and pair_row_offsets, and the per-token operations store_row (4 scatters of 16 dwords), load_row (4 gathers) and copy_token [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:95-112, 135-215, 224-281, 291-339]. store_block and transpose_16x16_epi32 are PR-3. The row-major group (row_major_row, store_row_major, load_row_major) and the conversion group (block_to_vnni, block_to_rows) are PR-4.

Follow the four call paths of this PR. save_k_impl calls page::set_k_row, which calls store_row [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3113-3119; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2010-2023]. The staging callback k_head_fn calls page::get_k_row, which calls load_row into the caller's scratch [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2747-2762; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2028-2040]. apply_page_tok takes page::k_packed and hands it to qk_group [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1972-1979; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1991-2001], and copy_storage_slot assigns the owner for a whole page and uses copy_token otherwise [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2286-2301]. page::k keeps its eight overloads but requires a row-major slot [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1924-1985].

Show only steps 3 and 4. store_row scatters one token's 64 dimension pairs into its column: 4 bytes into each of 64 lines, where the row-major store wrote 4 whole lines [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:286-304]. That is the per-token cost named in the PR body, and PR-3 replaces it with a whole-block store for runs of 16 tokens. Rows 1, 2 and 5 (the row-major form, block_to_vnni, block_to_rows) are PR-4.

Open the reader, because no base diagram draws its loop [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:57-126]. For each token block the live mask selects 16 lanes, each 64-byte pair row is loaded with a masked load so dead tokens are never read, the query's dimension pair is broadcast, and VDPBF16PS accumulates 16 scores at once [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:84-103]. A group wider than 16 heads is scored in passes of 16 [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:65-70]. The reader is checked against the row-major dotter for 4, 20 and 32 heads with masks that have holes [t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp:211-342].

Three lanes carry this PR. Main stores rows through set_k_row inside save_k's marks loop [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3092-3126]; the attention workers score every page of a VNNI slot with qk_group, because the dense AMX predicate carries the temporary gate && !k_vnni::layout_on [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1885-1887, 1962-1979]; the staging gather reads get_k_row on an attention worker or on main [src/tron/gof.cpp:203-213]. The helper lanes and the join are PR-3. The bits, the conversion and the rules R1 to R7 are PR-4.

The decision tree has two live nodes here: a VNNI slot stores each token through set_k_row, and a row-major slot through page::k().set [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3103-3122]. A non-bf16 K buffer is converted to bf16 on the stack first [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3116-3119]. Runs of 16, the bits and the hardware-attention branch are PR-3 and PR-4.

Point at the red dashed lane: after this PR save_k is the whole K store on main, one scatter store per token. pr.title: Add the VNNI K layout and its readers
pr.head: 82d05e94be

short_version: PR-1 (#4868) stores the saved key vectors (K) of 128-dimension attention heads in the VNNI-packed layout, behind a typed owner and typed views, and adds no AMX instruction.

The page introduces three data models (the typed K plane with its layout gate, the plane geometry with its index map, and the owner with its views) and three algorithms (the per-token store and load, the AVX-512 reader, and the scoring-path selection with its temporary gate).
Six base diagrams carry them, from the cache data model through the plane and the types to the operations and their call paths, and the ten other diagrams say what lands in PR-2, PR-3 and PR-4.

words.definition: DMA is direct memory access, the engine that moves a staging buffer to the FPGA card. A row view carries two compile-time flags: Aligned says the row starts at a 64-byte boundary, and Dma says the row lives in DMA memory. The K row operations load and store rows with unaligned vector instructions, so they do not require Aligned [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:219-228].
Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set of the CPU. Its tile multiply TDPBF16PS reads its right operand (the B operand) in the VNNI layout. This PR adds no AMX instruction.

The per-page scoring function of h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp. For one (query, page) pair it picks the dense AMX kernel or the software reader. In this PR every page of a VNNI slot takes the software reader qk_group [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1833-1979].

The threads that run the attention kernels of a layer. They read a page only after every minibatch that writes it counted its latch (upstream_kvs_ready) down. Idle attention workers also run the staging gather through help_drain_gof.

Advanced Vector Extensions, the CPU's 512-bit vector instruction set. One register holds 16 lanes of 32 bits. VDPBF16PS is its instruction that multiplies bf16 pairs and adds them in fp32. The reader qk_group, store_row and load_row are AVX-512 code.

bf16 is the 16-bit brain floating-point format of the stored K and V values. fp32 is the 32-bit float format in which the score kernels add. A bf16 shifted up by 16 bits is the exact fp32. fp16 is the 16-bit IEEE half format. An fp16 query is widened to fp32 once by the reader [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:10-12, 71-77].

16 consecutive page offsets of a page (BLOCK_TOKENS_16), page offsets 16 c .. 16 c + 15. A page has TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 = 4 blocks. A block's bytes are its 4 panels, 4 KiB in all [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:63-64, 74-75].
The in-place conversions of one 16-token block between its row-major form and its VNNI form. They land in PR-4 (#4901), not in this PR.
The unit of memory allocation of the KV cache. It owns the memory for a requested number of pages and hands out references to them [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:833].
model.hpp's per-operation answer, decided once per model, whether the FPGA scores the operation's K. PR-4 uses it in save_k to keep such blocks row-major. This PR does not read it in save_k.

The CMake job of .github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml. This PR adds -DTRON_K_VNNI=ON to its configure line, so the whole test suite runs on the VNNI layout there [.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:356].

In save_k, a K buffer row whose activation type is not bf16 is converted to a 64-byte-aligned bf16 row on the stack (named row) before set_k_row stores it [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3116-3119]. PR-3 (#4898) moves that conversion into store_k_block, where the stack array is conv[k_store_block][head_size], one row per token of a run.

book::append copies one book's tokens after another's, page by page through page::copy_from, which calls copy_storage_slot per storage slot. Both exist in main and are unchanged by this PR [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1247, 2322].

page::copy_storage_slot copies count tokens of one storage slot from another page. For a VNNI slot this PR copies a whole page as one owner assignment (dst_block.k = src_block.k) and every other range token by token with copy_token (load_row then store_row through a local row) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2286-2301; h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:331-339].

Prefill is prompt processing: many tokens per user per pass. Decode is generation: one token per user per step. PR-3's Note [Shared block save] measures the per-token store of this PR at 0.86 ms per layer in a prefill layer, and PR-3 (#4898) replaces it for runs of 16 tokens.

A full 64-token page that the query sees whole. main's AMX page kernel qk_rowmajor_128x4 processes it in one call (apply_dense_amx_page). In this PR that path is compiled out for VNNI slots by the temporary gate.

Dimensions 2 dp and 2 dp + 1 of one token, stored together in one 32-bit lane (a dword, DWORD_BYTES_4) [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:58-60]. The even value is in the low half of the dword and the odd value in the high half [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:80-81; h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:107-108].
32 dimensions = 16 dimension pairs (STEP_DIMS_32, STEP_PAIRS_16). A 128-dimension head has DIM_STEPS_4 = 4 steps [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:67-69].

main's per-token dot-product routine for a row-major K row (struct dotter in h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp), driven by the per-token loop of apply_page_tok. In this PR it is compiled only for row-major slots.
A speculation model whose KV storage is one extra physical slot of the book (eagle_storage_offset). This PR does not change it. PR-4 (#4901) adds a K layout state entry for it.

book::fill_random is a test-only fill of every kv_block with random bf16 values, and fill_storage_slot is its body per storage slot. It is the one documented exception to the typed access rule: for a VNNI slot it takes the plane address through detail::k_vnni_access [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1291, 1716-1726].

The end of one forward pass on the main thread, after the plugin's run() (the forward function of the generated model code) returned and wait_for_coop_gof drained the staging gather. PR-4 converts completed blocks there. This PR converts nothing.
Field-programmable gate array, the card that runs hardware attention and receives K and V rows by DMA.
A group of four consecutive tokens. The staging gather (gof::populate) copies their K and V rows into a buffer that DMA moves to the FPGA card.
Attention scored on the FPGA for an operation. PR-4 adds a policy that keeps short-run blocks row-major under it. This PR has no such policy.

The constexpr function that gives the element index of K[token][dim] inside the plane: (((s * 4 + c) * 16 + dp) * 16 + t) * 2 + j [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:105-112]. The worked example (token 37, dimension 70) gives element 5226.

page_info is the per-token record the scheduler builds for the staging gather. Its k_head_fn callback returns a pointer to the token's K row for one slot and KV head. This PR adds a scratch argument: for a VNNI slot the callback gathers the row into the caller's 64-byte-aligned scratch (256 bytes per head) and returns the scratch [h/tron/gof.hpp:61-78; h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2747-2762].

page::k_packed(slot, kv_head): the read-only typed view (k_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128>) of one page's K plane, VNNI slots only. It is the argument of the reader qk_group [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1991-2001].

The page's two atomic bit arrays per storage slot: one bit per page offset (saved rows) and one bit per 16-token block (converted blocks). They land in PR-4 (#4901). In this PR the page keeps no K layout state.

Helpers that build a read-only row view from a bf16 pointer or from a rank-1 bf16 view that keeps its own flags (k_source_row), and a writable row view from a bf16 pointer (k_destination_row). They neither check alignment nor copy data [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:232-253].

Inside detail::kv_block, k_storage is a std::conditional_t that names k_vnni_tensor<page_size, head_size> when k_vnni::layout_on<head_size> holds and the bf16 array native_k_storage otherwise. The member k has that type. Both hold page_size * head_size bf16 values [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2526-2536].

A friend helper with one static function, plane(view), that returns the view's raw pointer to the plane's first element. It is the only route from a view to a plane address, for the typed operations, the reader qk_group and the test-only fill [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:209-215].

TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 in the environment prevents use of the AMX kernels at run time. With the option on, the switch keeps the layout and the reader: it changes no score and no visit path for 128-dimension heads in this PR [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:707-713]. AMX-on names a run without the switch, and AMX-off a run with it. AMX dispatch (TRON_AMX_DISPATCH) is the CMake option that compiles the AMX kernels. This PR does not require it: the option-on build passes its tests with AMX dispatch off [PR body, Builds and tests].

One key/value head of grouped-query attention (GQA: several query heads share one key/value head). kv_mul is the number of query heads per KV head: 4 for qwen3-4b and llama-3.1-8b, 3 for llama-3.2-3b, and 8 for qwen-3-30b-a3b. The reader scores a group of more than 16 heads in passes of 16.
A KV page is 64 consecutive tokens of KV storage allocated by the cache (page_size = 64). The page struct is a lightweight reference into a book [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1826-1828].
The struct that holds the K plane and the V plane of one (storage slot, KV head, page). This PR types its K plane [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2519-2536].

kv_slot_id selects one persistent K/V storage region of the book, usually one per layer [h/tron/attention_ids.hpp:23]. A storage slot (kv_storage_offset) is the absolute physical slot offset in the book's allocation [h/tron/models/common.hpp:240].
One transformer layer of the model. Each layer stores its K and V into its own slot of the KV cache.

k_vnni::layout_on<head_size> is true only for 128-dimension heads and only when the option TRON_K_VNNI is defined. It depends only on the storage geometry, so every reader and writer of a slot selects the same layout [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:95-101].

A 64-bit word with one bit per page offset. apply_page_tok sets the bit of every relevant token during its loop and hands the word to qk_group, which reads only those tokens [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1933, 1962-1963, 1976-1979].

The main thread runs the generated run() of a plugin (the generated model code), including save_k. The main helpers are its helper threads (run_main_help). In this PR save_k runs on main alone. PR-3 (#4898) shares its K store with the helpers.

mark_k_complete records in the page that a token's K is saved. upstream_kvs_ready is the per-slot latch (a countdown object) that downstream minibatches wait on. save_k counts it down after its stores. Both exist in main and are unchanged here [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3126, 3134-3135].
The per-token loop of save_k_impl over the minibatch's items. For each token it stores the K rows of every KV head and then calls mark_k_complete (the mark) [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3091-3132].
One chunk of a forward pass's token jobs that the forward runs together. save_k stores the K rows of one minibatch, and downstream minibatches wait on its latch [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3133-3135].
A deliberate code change that a test must catch. The PR body reports one: removing the per-head scratch offset in gof::populate makes the populate case of t_phase1_integration fail.

The design comment in h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp that says what the layout is, who writes it, who reads it, how each of the six consumers of a VNNI slot changes, and that the kill switch keeps the layout [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:651-713].

words.term: Note [Row-major tail block] / row-major tail block
words.definition: A 16-token block of a VNNI plane whose rows stay row-major until all 16 rows are saved, then converted in place. It lands in PR-4 (#4901). In this PR every row goes straight into the VNNI column.

words.term: Note [Shared block save] / shared block save / window
words.definition: PR-3's design: a run of 16 tokens is stored as one whole block, and the main helpers claim work units of the store through a window of counters. Main waits for every helper to finish its claims (the join) before it marks the tokens. None of it is in this PR.
The page functions that publish the saved-row bits and the block bit. They land in PR-4 (#4901).

The CMake option, default OFF, that selects VNNI-packed K storage for every 128-dimension head [CMakeLists.txt:47]. Its compile definition is PUBLIC on the tron target and on the generated model objects, so every translation unit that touches a KV page sees the same layout [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:232-233, 336-341]. It stays off in every build preset until PR-4.

k_vnni_tensor<64, 128> owns one K plane as a 64-byte-aligned bf16 array, trivial to construct, copy and destroy. k_vnni_view<T, 64, 128> refers to that plane and computes element addresses. Its at(token, dim) reads one element and cannot write it. Views come only from an owner's as_view(), and a writable view converts to a read-only one, never back [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:135-201].
A token's position inside its 64-token page, 0 to 63. In the VNNI plane the offset decides the token's block (offset / 16) and its column (offset % 16).

The row-major K views. kv_block::k_view() is the plane as a [token][element] view, k_at(i_page) is one token's row, and page::k(slot, kv_head) returns the kv_block's k_view. page::k(slot, kv_head, j).set(row) writes one token's row. In this PR all of them exist only when layout_on is false [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1924-1985, 2554-2572].

One 64-byte line of a panel: one dimension pair for 16 consecutive tokens, 32 bf16 = 16 dwords (ROW_ELEMS_32, ROW_DWORDS_16) [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:61-62, 70-72]. The 16 pair rows of a panel are 64 bytes apart [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:258-259, 272].

The address arithmetic of store_row and load_row. pair_base gives the byte address of dimension pair 0 of step s for a token (its column in panel (s, c)). pair_row_offsets lists the 16 pair rows of a panel, 16 dwords apart, as the index vector of the scatter and the gather [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:261-281].

One (dimension step s, token block c) cell of the plane: 16 pair rows of 64 bytes = 1 KiB (PANEL_BYTES_1024). A plane has N_PANELS_16 = 16 panels, and a panel is exactly one AMX B tile [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:26-27, 74-77].
The deferred conversion list of save_k and the forward-end function that drains it. They land in PR-4 (#4901).
K for one KV head of one page: 64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB, the same bytes as the row-major plane [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:21-30].

PR is a GitHub pull request of the tron repository. PR 4424 (branch jhan-amx-vnniK) is the original change that the four PRs of the stack replace: PR-1 #4868, PR-2 #4887, PR-3 #4898 and PR-4 #4901, each based on the previous one.
A run with a prompt length of 1024 tokens (runtron --prompt-length). The performance cells of the PR body use prompt 1024 and prompt 8192.

k_vnni::qk_group in h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp: the AVX-512 routine that scores a query group against the live tokens of one VNNI-packed page, one token per vector lane. One 64-byte load supplies one dimension pair of 16 tokens, the query's pair is broadcast, and VDPBF16PS accumulates 16 scores at once, so there is no per-token gather [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:57-127].

qk_rowmajor_128x4 is main's AMX QK kernel for a row-major K page: it puts the K page on the left and transposes the score matrix after the multiply. qk_vnni_128x4 is the AMX kernel that reads the VNNI plane as its B operand and lands in PR-2 (#4887).

The step that rearranges a token's query rows into the AMX operand format (pack_q_group_128x4 in main). In this PR it still runs once per token for a VNNI slot, and no kernel consumes it. The kill switch skips it [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1633-1634, 1688-1696].

A typed view of one token's 128 K values in dimension order, read-only (const_k_row_view) or writable (k_row_view), carrying the caller's Aligned and Dma flags. It is the argument type of set_k_row, get_k_row, store_row and load_row [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:224-228].
One row of head_size bf16 values per token, indexed [token * head_size + dimension]. Every head size other than 128 keeps this layout, and so does a 128-dimension head when the option is off.
tron's command-line tool, the binary the PR body's performance and token-identity runs use.

The function of h/tron/models/model.hpp that stores the K rows of one minibatch into the KV cache. The two save_k overloads forward to save_k_impl. In this PR save_k_impl stores each token's row with page::set_k_row for a VNNI slot and with page::k().set for a row-major slot [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3077-3153].

_mm512_i32scatter_epi32 writes the 16 dwords of one register to a base plus 16 offsets, and _mm512_i32gather_epi32 reads 16 dwords from such addresses. store_row issues 4 scatters per token (one per dimension step) and touches 64 lines. load_row is the inverse with 4 gathers.
The thread that runs the scheduler of h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp between forward passes. It defines the page_info callbacks of the staging gather, which other threads run.
The whole-block store of a run of 16 tokens: 16 rows transposed in registers and written as whole lines. Both land in PR-3 (#4898).

The layout-agnostic page accessors that this PR adds. set_k_row writes one token's row (a const_k_row_view) into whichever layout the slot uses: store_row for a VNNI slot, memcpy for a row-major one. get_k_row is the inverse with load_row [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2010-2063].

The copy of K and V rows of one GOF into the buffer that DMA moves to the FPGA. It runs on an idle attention worker (help_drain_gof) or on main (wait_for_coop_gof). This PR gives it a K scratch array beside the V scratch, with one row per KV head [src/tron/gof.cpp:203-213].

store_row scatters one token's 128-dimension row into its column of the plane: 4 scatters of 16 dwords, one per dimension step, touching only that token's 64 pair slots. load_row gathers the row back. Both check the token index [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:291-322].

The four tests of this PR with new or changed cases. Two more test files, t_gof_dma and t_gof_staging_leaks, only give their k_head_fn lambdas the new scratch argument. t_k_vnni_layout is new, with four cases: the index anchors, the exact scrambled store and load, the reader against the dotter, and page rows through store, load and append. t_llama_unit gains the compile checks of the type model, a 32-head compile case and a save_k case. t_phase1_integration's populate case stages K rows through the scratch. t_amx_dispatch_dtype expects no dense kernel call under the option.

The term && !k_vnni::layout_on<operation_head_size> that this PR adds to the dense-page AMX predicate of apply_page_tok. It keeps the dense AMX path out of VNNI slots until PR-2 adds the AMX kernel, so every VNNI-packed page takes the reader [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1885-1887].

Decode throughput in tokens per second per user. The PR body measures a decode TPS loss of 6.4 % at prompt 1024 and 11.6 % at prompt 8192 against main, and attributes it to the temporary gate, which sends the dense pages that main's AMX kernel serves to the reader.
The in-register 16 x 16 transpose that store_block uses. It lands in PR-3 (#4898).
The lock on the scheduler's token tree, held for the tree work between forward passes (clear_kv_complete_at, copy_from).
The inference program under test (the positron-ai/tron repository). Its C++ code lives in namespace tron.

VDPBF16PS is the AVX-512 instruction that multiplies bf16 pairs and adds them in fp32. The reader uses it. TDPBF16PS is the AMX tile multiply that reads the same pair layout as its B operand. No PR-1 code uses it.

Vector Neural Network Instructions layout: two consecutive dimensions of one token are adjacent in memory, and one 64-byte line holds that dimension pair for 16 consecutive tokens. It is the B-operand format of the AMX tile multiply. VNNI-packed means stored in this layout.

The two ends of the cooperative staging gather: idle attention workers run queued GOFs through help_drain_gof, and main drains the rest at the forward end through wait_for_coop_gof. Both exist in main and are unchanged here [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3239, 3252].
tron's record label for the K rows after rope (the rotary position embedding), logged by save_k_impl through log_intermediate [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3094].

The example the three source pages trace through every diagram: the K plane of storage slot 5, KV head 0, page 7, and inside it token 37, dimension 70, which the index map places at element 5226 (panel #10, pair row 3, dword 5).

walkthrough.say: PR-1 is the first of the four PRs that split PR 4424. It stores K of 128-dimension heads in the VNNI-packed layout behind a typed owner and typed views, adds the AVX-512 reader and the FPGA staging gather as the two consumers, and adds no AMX instruction. The CMake option TRON_K_VNNI is off in every build preset, so every preset keeps the row-major layout [CMakeLists.txt:47]. With the option off, the five layout-independent tests pass [PR body, Builds and tests]. The compile definition is PUBLIC, so the generated model objects see the same layout as the tron library [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:232-233, 336-341].

Start at the kv_block card at the right: its k member becomes k_storage, a std::conditional_t that names k_vnni_tensor (the owner type, introduced at k_vnni-b2) for a VNNI slot and the bf16 array native_k_storage otherwise, with two static_asserts for a trivial type and the same byte count [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2526-2536]. The arrow label is the layout gate k_vnni::layout_on, true only for 128-dimension heads and only with the option [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:95-101]. The row views k_view and k_at exist only on the row-major branch [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2554-2571]. The page's two bit arrays in the middle card are PR-4, so skip them.

Point at the plane: 64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB, the same bytes as the row-major plane [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:21-30]. Walk the containment. A plane is 16 panels of 1 KiB, one per (dimension step s, token block c). A panel is 16 pair rows of 64 bytes. A pair row is one dimension pair for 16 tokens [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:56-77]. Then run the worked example through k_vnni::index: token 37, dimension 70 lands at element 5226 [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:105-112]. The orange frame (block 2 still row-major) is PR-4.

Use the five levels to say the same thing from the top. Level 1: the K of page 7 for slot 5 is one plane per KV head. Level 2: a dimension step cuts the columns and a token block cuts the rows, so a panel is one cell of the 4 x 4 cut. Level 3: a pair is two consecutive dimensions of one token. Level 4: a pair row holds one pair of 16 tokens. Level 5: a dword is one token's pair, with the even value in the low half [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:24-29, 58-60, 80-81]. The hand-computed anchors of this map are the first test case [t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp:101-118]. The last line, the row-major form of a block, is PR-4.

This is the answer to Ben's 2026-09-21 request for typed access. k_vnni_tensor owns the bytes. Its as_view() is the only source of a view, and as_view() on a temporary is deleted [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:180-201]. k_vnni_view reads through at(token, dim) and has no element write, no pointer constructor and no data() [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:135-170]. detail::k_vnni_access::plane is the one route to the raw address, open to store_row, load_row, copy_token, the reader qk_group and the test-only fill_storage_slot [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:209-215; h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:83; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1721-1722]. The transfer rows const_k_row_view and k_row_view carry one token's 128 values in dimension order [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:224-253], and qk_vnni_128x4 in the grey box is PR-2.

Read the list group by group. Groups 1 to 4 are in this PR: the gate and the index map, the views and the access route, the transfer rows with pair_base and pair_row_offsets, and the per-token operations store_row (4 scatters of 16 dwords), load_row (4 gathers) and copy_token [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:95-112, 135-215, 224-281, 291-339]. store_block and transpose_16x16_epi32 are PR-3. The row-major group (row_major_row, store_row_major, load_row_major) and the conversion group (block_to_vnni, block_to_rows) are PR-4.

Follow the four call paths of this PR. save_k_impl calls page::set_k_row, which calls store_row [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3113-3119; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2010-2023]. The staging callback k_head_fn calls page::get_k_row, which calls load_row into the caller's scratch [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2747-2762; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2028-2040]. apply_page_tok takes page::k_packed and hands it to qk_group [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1972-1979; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1991-2001], and copy_storage_slot assigns the owner for a whole page and uses copy_token otherwise [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2286-2301]. page::k keeps its eight overloads but requires a row-major slot [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1924-1985].

Show only steps 3 and 4. store_row scatters one token's 64 dimension pairs into its column: 4 bytes into each of 64 lines, where the row-major store wrote 4 whole lines [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:283-304]. That is the per-token cost named in the PR body, and PR-3 replaces it with a whole-block store for runs of 16 tokens. Rows 1, 2 and 5 (the row-major form, block_to_vnni, block_to_rows) are PR-4.

Open the reader. No base diagram draws its loop [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:57-127]. For each token block the 16 bits of the live mask for that block select the lanes. Each 64-byte pair row is loaded with that mask, so a dead token's storage is never read. The query's dimension pair is broadcast, and VDPBF16PS accumulates 16 scores at once [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:84-105]. A group wider than 16 heads is scored in passes of 16 [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:65-70]. The reader is checked against the row-major dotter for 4, 20 and 32 heads, with masks that have holes [t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp:206-343].

Three lanes carry this PR. Main stores rows through set_k_row inside save_k's marks loop [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3091-3132]. The attention workers score every page of a VNNI slot with qk_group. The dense AMX predicate carries the temporary gate && !k_vnni::layout_on, so no page of a VNNI slot reaches the AMX kernel [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1885-1887, 1962-1979]. The staging gather reads get_k_row on an attention worker or on main [src/tron/gof.cpp:203-213]. The helper lanes and the join are PR-3. The bits, the conversion and the rules R1 to R7 are PR-4.

The decision tree has two live nodes here: a VNNI slot stores each token through set_k_row, and a row-major slot through page::k().set [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3103-3122]. A non-bf16 K buffer is converted to bf16 on the stack first, in the array the diagram calls conv and this PR calls row [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3116-3119]. Runs of 16, the bits and the hardware-attention branch are PR-3 and PR-4.

Point at the red dashed lane: after this PR save_k is the whole K store on main, one set_k_row per token, 4 scatters each. The Note that PR-3 adds quotes 0.86 ms per layer for that store (measured 2026-09-14 on delphi-3bda with qwen3-4b, 8 users, prompt 1024). That cost is why PR-3 adds the helper lanes and the whole-block store.

Close with what Ben should verify: the compile checks of the type model [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:421-429], the four cases of t_k_vnni_layout, the populate case with its mutation check [t/t_phase1_integration.cpp:845-922], the PUBLIC compile definition [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:232-233, 336-341] and the CI lane that builds with the option on [.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:356]. The kill switch keeps the layout and the reader, so it changes no scoring path in this PR [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:707-713]. The PR body measures a decode TPS loss of 6.4 % at prompt 1024 and 11.6 % at prompt 8192 against main and attributes it to the temporary gate. PR-2 removes the gate with the AMX kernel.
